MetaStrip draft

The row of small mono facts at the foot of a hero: a dashed top rule, then a wrapping list of facts — each a key rendered by the library's Eyebrow, followed by an optional value in fg/mute — or in the accent, with valueTone. Text only, no states; the parent places it.

Variants: dim accent · A11y: pending

No states: nothing hovers, nothing focuses (RFC §3.3). The keys are real Eyebrows (the library's first component-to-component dependency, §3.5): a change to the Eyebrow is a change to the MetaStrip. The dashed rule is the browser's CSS dashed — the Figma set's [3, 3] dash array is a stand-in for it (§3.4).

RFC: MetaStrip.rfc.md · Figma node: 106:29

Guidelines

Golden rules

  1. A list of facts, read fact by fact. One <ul role="list"> with one <li> per entry of items, in order: a screen reader announces "list, 3 items" and steps through them (RFC §4.1, §7 Q8). An empty items renders nothing.
  2. The key is an Eyebrow. Every key renders the library's Eyebrow — the type/meta recipe in capitals, by CSS — so the strip never restates it (RFC §7 Q3). Write the key in its own casing.
  3. One tone per strip. dim (the default) or accent, which follows data-accent — forwarded to every key (RFC §3.1, §7 Q4). The values have their own tone, valueTone: fg/mute by default, or accent (RFC §3.1, §7 checkpoint rows 2026-10-14). Both apply to the whole strip.
  4. Text only — the parent places it. The strip ships its dashed top rule, the 24px above its text and its own gaps; no outer margin, width or alignment. A slot class product-side spaces it from what follows (RFC §3.4).

Do

  • Pass the facts as data: items={[{ label: "Read time", value: "~15 min" }]} (RFC §3.1).
  • Omit value for a key alone ({ label: "Patch-stable" }) — no empty value, no placeholder (RFC §3.4).
  • Use tone="accent" when the keys should follow the page accent; keep the default dim otherwise (RFC §7 Q4).
  • Use valueTone="accent" where the values are the highlights (the role guides: level, read time, patch); keep the default mute elsewhere (RFC §7 checkpoint rows 2026-10-14).
  • Place it as the last child of the hero's text column and let the column set its width (RFC §2.3).

Don't

  • Don't put a symbol rating in a value (★★☆): write the level as a word (RFC §7 Q5).
  • Don't add separators between facts — the gap separates them; a · typed inside a value stays content (RFC §7 Q6).
  • Don't override the strip's size, tracking or gaps product-side — one recipe (RFC §7 Q2, Q7).
  • Don't put interactive content in a value: the strip is static text (RFC §4.2).

Props

PropTypeDefaultOptionalNote
items ReadonlyArray<{ label: ReactNode; value?: ReactNode }> — no the facts, in reading order, one <li> each (RFC §3.1). label is the key, rendered by the library's Eyebrow (§7 Q3); value is optional inline content after it — omitted (or null) for a key alone, then no space and no value span. Product content, passed through untouched. Empty → the component renders nothing. `label`, not `key`: key is reserved by React
tone "dim" | "accent" dim yes the key colour for the whole strip, forwarded to every key's Eyebrow as its own tone (§7 Q4): fg/dim by default, or accent/default, which follows the accent axis. One tone per strip
valueTone "mute" | "accent" mute yes the value colour for the whole strip (RFC §3.1, §7 adoption-checkpoint rows 2026-10-14: « P1 couleur: 1C accent · P1 portee: Roles seulement (option) »): fg/mute by default — the value span carries no modifier and inherits the strip's colour — or accent/default, which follows the accent axis (the value span adds ll-meta-strip-value--accent). Independent of tone (the keys'). The name is proposed by the implementing session, for the design lead's confirmation at PR. No other prop — no children, size, as, separator (§7 Q6), rating (§7 Q5), className or layout prop

Accessibility pending

Semantic structure
Exactly one <ul class="ll-meta-strip" role="list"> holding one <li class="ll-meta-strip-item"> per entry of items, in order — no wrapper, nothing between two li (RFC §3.4, §4.1, §7 Q8). Each li holds the key's Eyebrow (<span class="ll-eyebrow ll-eyebrow--{tone}">) and, when a value is present, one literal space then <span class="ll-meta-strip-value"> (plus ll-meta-strip-value--accent under valueTone="accent"), so the DOM text reads "label value". A list, not a dl: two of the site's content shapes have no definition. No heading semantics, no live region, no accessible name on the list, no ARIA attribute beyond role="list". The uppercase of the key is the Eyebrow's CSS text-transform, so assistive tech reads the author's casing. Empty items renders nothing, never an empty list.
Keyboard
Nothing to do: no interactive element, nothing focusable — no a, button, input or tabindex is rendered by the component (RFC §3.3, §4.2). Interactive content in a value is not expected; if the product passes one it keeps its own semantics and focus, product-side.
Decisions
role="list" is explicit because WebKit (Safari + VoiceOver) drops list semantics from a list styled list-style: none (RFC §4.3 — the lot-1 orchestrator's decision, 2026-10-13, for the design lead's review). Contrast is computed by the contrast gate from resolved tokens over pairs already declared in contrast-pairs.json — the component adds none: the value is fg/mute on bg/default, or accent/default on bg/default under valueTone="accent" (the pair the Eyebrow's accent tone already declares, scored once per accent); the key, through the Eyebrow, is fg/dim on bg/default and accent/default on bg/default, scored once per accent; 11px is normal-size text (WCAG 1.4.3, 4.5:1). The dashed top rule is decoration, not an information-bearing boundary, so WCAG 1.4.11 does not apply and no line/rule pair is declared. No rating and no separator are rendered (§7 Q5, Q6), so nothing is aria-hidden. Text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12): no fixed height, no clipping, wrapping rows; the 0.06em tracking and 1.4 line-height are the type/meta tokens (§7 Q2) — a design arbitration already made, not an accessibility defect to reopen.
Notes
Implemented per RFC §4; this status moves to pass only through the accessibility engine gate, never by assertion.
